exposure: Sibling pairs discordant for both mode of delivery and T1D
Mode of delivery: Unassisted vaginal delivery, Instrumental vaginal delivery (IVD), Emergency CS, Elective CS
cohort: All singleton live births in Sweden between 1982 and 2009 (N = 2,638,083)
finding: While an association between elective CS, IVD, and increased risk of childhood T1D was observed in the full cohort, this association became nonsignificant after accounting for familial confounding in the sibling-control analysis.
mod_finding: This study found a small association between elective cesarean section, instrumental vaginal delivery, and type 1 diabetes in offspring, but suggests that the findings may be due to familial confounders rather than causal effects of mode of delivery.
